- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. h13.

**`*markdown.service` (the only implementation) — constructed once by `markdown.NewService(...)` inside `apiv1.NewAPIV1Service` — held by `APIV1Service`, `RSSService`, and `memopayload.Runner`.**

### The interface
`markdown.Service` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:31` (ExtractAll, ExtractTags, ExtractProperties, RenderMarkdown, RenderHTML, GenerateSnippet, ValidateContent, RenameTag).

### Implementations
Exactly one concrete type: the unexported `service` struct wrapping a `goldmark.Markdown` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:58`). No mocks, fakes, or alternate implementations exist in the repo — a grep for other `ExtractAll`/`RenderHTML` methods returns only these. (Inside `RenderMarkdown`/`RenameTag` it delegates to `renderer.NewMarkdownRenderer()` at `internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go`, but that renderer is a plain struct, not behind this interface.)

### Construction
- Runtime: `markdown.NewService(markdown.WithTagExtension(), markdown.WithMentionExtension())` — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51`, called from `NewAPIV1Service`, which is itself called once in `server/server.go:76`. So a single instance with GFM + tag + mention extensions exists per server process.
- Tests: same call with the same two options in `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44-46`.

### Holders
| Holder | Field | How it gets the instance |
|---|---|---|
